summary: FIELDSHIFT is a farmer-focused decision-support concept that aims to help farmers adapt to changing climate conditions using NASA Earth observation data. The proposed tool combines information on rainfall, temperature, soil moisture and vegetation health with local soil conditions, crop characteristics and farmers’ needs. It compares different crop rotation strategies, including existing practices, to identify possible alternatives and their benefits, risks and limitations. Designed with Kerala’s agricultural context in mind, FIELDSHIFT aims to make satellite-based information easier to understand and support more informed, climate-resilient farming decisions.
details: FIELDSHIFT – Adapting Farms with NASA Data FIELDSHIFT is a farmer-focused decision-support concept developed by Team SPACETECHX for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project aims to connect NASA Earth observation data with local agricultural information to help farmers understand changing environmental conditions and make better crop rotation decisions. 1. Problem We Address Farmers face several challenges due to changing climate conditions, including rising temperatures, unpredictable rainfall, water shortages, soil moisture changes and declining soil health. Choosing the right crop rotation is difficult because different crops have different water requirements, soil needs and growing seasons. NASA provides valuable Earth observation data, but this information can be difficult for farmers to understand and apply in everyday farming. 2. Our Proposed Solution FIELDSHIFT aims to convert complex satellite-based environmental information into simple and useful agricultural insights. It combines NASA Earth observation data, local soil information, crop characteristics and farmer priorities to compare different crop rotation strategies. 3. NASA Data Sources Our proposed system considers eight NASA data sources: - NASA POWER – Temperature, precipitation and solar radiation. - GPM – Rainfall patterns and extreme precipitation. - SMAP – Surface and root-zone soil moisture. - ECOSTRESS – Land surface temperature and evapotranspiration. - Landsat – Vegetation condition and land-use changes. - MODIS – Vegetation indices and seasonal patterns. - GRACE / GRACE-FO – Regional water-storage changes. - SRTM – Elevation and terrain information for erosion-risk screening. These datasets are proposed inputs and have not yet been downloaded or analysed in our current prototype. 4. How FIELDSHIFT Works The proposed workflow has seven stages: 1. The farmer selects the field location and enters soil type, existing crop rotation, water availability and farming priorities. 2. Relevant NASA environmental datasets are collected through official NASA portals and APIs. 3. The collected data is cleaned, checked, standardised and prepared for analysis. 4. NASA observations are combined with local soil characteristics, crop requirements and farmer preferences. 5. Environmental conditions such as rainfall changes, temperature trends, soil moisture, vegetation health and water stress are assessed. 6. Three crop rotation strategies are compared using transparent criteria and farmer-selected priorities. 7. Results are presented through a simple dashboard with explanations, possible benefits, limitations and confidence levels. 5. Crop Rotation Strategies FIELDSHIFT compares three strategies: Strategy A – Existing Rotation: The farmer's current crop rotation, used as the baseline. Strategy B – Legume and Cover-Crop Rotation: Considers nitrogen fixation by legumes, soil protection, organic matter improvement and erosion reduction. Strategy C – Diversified, Deep-Rooted and Drought-Tolerant Rotation: Explores crop diversification, deeper root systems and crops that can better tolerate dry conditions. The strategies are compared based on water requirements, soil health, nitrogen contribution, erosion reduction, pest-cycle disruption, growing-season suitability, market suitability and farmer preferences. 6. Proposed Dashboard Our concept dashboard allows farmers to select their field, enter soil and water information, choose farming priorities and compare the three rotation strategies. It is designed to present environmental indicators and explain why a particular strategy may or may not suit the selected field. The current dashboard is a concept prototype mock-up. Its displayed values, charts and imagery are illustrative and are not actual NASA measurements. 7. Benefits and Expected Impact FIELDSHIFT aims to support better-informed crop rotation planning, improved soil management, more efficient water use, reduced periods of exposed soil and better understanding of seasonal climate risks. It also aims to make NASA Earth observation data more accessible to farming communities and encourage sustainable, climate-resilient agricultural practices. 8. Creativity, Limitations and Future Development The main innovation of FIELDSHIFT is connecting space-based environmental observations with practical crop rotation decisions through a farmer-friendly approach. The project combines satellite information, local agricultural knowledge and individual farming priorities rather than presenting technical satellite data alone. Currently, the project has a concept and dashboard mock-up. NASA data integration, environmental analysis, strategy scoring and farmer and expert testing are planned future developments. Local soil tests, ground observations and agricultural expert review will be essential before providing actual crop recommendations. FIELDSHIFT is designed to support farmers' decisions, not replace their knowledge or professional agricultural advice.
